The test `test_asyncio_close_leak` checks whether the cleanup of async I/O loops is handled correctly after they are closed. It creates and closes ten AsyncIOMainLoop instances using asyncio interfaces and expects there to be one dangling entry in the `_ioloop_for_asyncio` map afterward. However, the test fails because it finds 10 instead of 1.

Upon examining the `close` method of `tornado.ioloop.IOLoop`, we observe that it only removes the current loop from `_ioloops_for_watcher` but does not clean up `_ioloop_for_asyncio`. Consequently, every time a new loop is created and closed in the test, an entry is added to `_ioloop_for_asyncio`, leading to the incorrect result.

Conclusion: The test `test_asyncio_close_leak` checks whether the cleanup of async I/O loops is handled correctly after they are closed. It fails because the `close` method of `tornado.ioloop.IOLoop` does not clean up `_ioloop_for_asyncio`, leading to an incorrect result.

Suggested fixes:
```
tornado.ioloop.IOLoop.close(self)
```
